description: NAD+ is the oxidised form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, the central electron carrier of cellular redox metabolism and the substrate for sirtuin and PARP enzyme families. It is a standard reagent in cellular-metabolism, enzymology and ageing-biology research, supplied as the oxidised (NAD⁺) form rather than the reduced NADH form.

faq.question: Is this NAD+ or NADH?
faq.answer: Oxidised NAD+ (CAS 53-84-9), molecular weight ~663.4 Da. The reduced form NADH is a separate reagent and is not supplied under this listing.

faq.question: Why is NAD+ relevant to ageing research?
faq.answer: Because NAD+ is the cofactor consumed by sirtuins and PARPs, so its measured availability is a common endpoint in cellular-ageing research models. We make no human-health claim for this reagent.

faq.question: How should NAD+ be stored?
faq.answer: Store the powder sealed and desiccated at 2–8°C, protected from light and moisture. Prepare solutions fresh: NAD+ hydrolyses in aqueous solution and is degraded more quickly at neutral-to-alkaline pH.
